name: Amber Brown
lede: Amber Brown is a warm, reddish brown from Ridgway's 1912 chart, called Kitsune-iro, fox-color, in Japanese tradition.

sections.title: A fox-colored brown
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 plate III gives this brown the name Amber Brown, hue 13, tone k, and the ISCC-NBS system of 1955 files a close match in its block 54 [1]. Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary also carries it, first recorded in 1892 [1]. In Japan the same hue is called Kitsune-iro, written 狐色 and meaning fox-color, after the reddish coat of the Japanese fox [1].

The nearest named colors on file are [[orange-brown]], [[sudan-brown]], [[earth]] and [[army-brown]], at 3.6, 3.6, 4.5 and 4.8 ΔE [1]. Among named browns it sits beside [[amber]] and [[umber]] [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this brown in 1,371 of 23,781 paintings, 5.8 percent, among the more common matches we track, as photographed [2]. The earliest dated match is a funerary papyrus of Tayuhenutmut, dated to about 1069 BCE in our archive, nearly three thousand years before either the Ridgway or Maerz and Paul records, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2]. It peaks around 1420, at 3.8 times the archive's overall rate, and Otto van Veen carries it in seven of his 15 paintings here, far above his own museums' baseline [2]. Inside a painting it most often plays a mid-tone, in 53 percent of its appearances [2].
